correctness.rationale: The site-generated cyclic space and its orthogonal complement both reduce the loss generator, with Hermitian dynamics on the complement. For an eigenvector u of K in the bright space, Im(lambda)||u||^2=-gamma|<v,u>|^2. A real eigenvalue would force orthogonality to v and then to every A^k v since J is real and nonzero, which contradicts brightness. Jordan blocks do not alter decay to zero on the finite bright space. Hence I/N gives capture rank/N, not the capture of a coherent uniform vector or an arbitrary localized state. Schur complementation gives the root determinant ratio P_(h+1)/P_h and the full product with P_k exponents (b-1)b^(h-k) for 1<=k<=h; no size disappears for b>=2. The Chebyshev roots are indexed by j/(k+1), with cos injective on (0,pi); reduction gives each reduced denominator 2 through h+2 exactly once per reduced fraction. No eigenvector can vanish on all leaves, by the eigen-equations inducting inwards. Rooted automorphism transitivity then gives nonzero projector diagonal at a fixed leaf for each eigenspace, so the leaf cyclic rank counts distinct eigenvalues, never multiplicities. Uniform level vectors give a Jacobi block with nonzero off-diagonals sqrt(b) and cyclic first vector at the root. This yields both ranks, independent of positive loss rate, and the standard summatory-totient estimate gives the claimed depth asymptotic. For the star h=1 the ranks are 3 and 2, respectively. There is no parameter-uniform finite-time assertion.

originality.rationale: The exact operative leaf-rank claim is demonstrably covered, not merely suggested by neighboring Cayley-tree spectra. In the distinct indexed two-leaf result 2026/11/2/SCOPE-two-leaf-coherent-capture-on-complete-branching-trees-an-exact-t--5d10e1c82c34, proof steps 1–2 explicitly count the same reduced-angle spectrum and prove every eigenvalue visible from one leaf; the proof states the exact single-leaf rank D(L). Its two-leaf increment needs b>=3, but its one-leaf steps only use b-1>0, the level Jacobi blocks and transitivity, and work unchanged for b=2. Novo et al.'s general single-trap projection principle converts that evaluated rank immediately to capture D(h)/N for I/N; the same work already treats root reduction to a path for the binary case, and replacing sqrt(2) by sqrt(b) gives the arbitrary-b root rank without further spectral work. The asymptotic is the classical summatory-totient estimate. Thus the corpus covers the leaf result itself and the remaining assertions follow directly, rather than the original result being established only by a generic formula with an unevaluated site measure. This is a statement-coverage determination, not an inference of historical priority or dependence from record dates.
